--- PART 1/4 ---

RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "We have measured parent behavior probes: starts with ten externally supplied CC rounds, then probe for 24 rounds. Parent performance: - one_D_TFT: after 10 CC, TFT defects once then copies. Parent recovers perfectly, score 2.875 (high). Good. - four_D_TFT: TFT defects 4 then copies. Parent not recovered, score 0.9167. Bad."
STRATEGY: Parent is a TFT-like policy that retaliates and occasionally probes; simulated against one_D_TFT, four_D_TFT, four_D_ALLC, sustained_D, periodic_D; changed by adding forgiveness after long defection runs, non-responsiveness detection, and endgame defection.

--- PART 2/4 ---

So it never recovered in those 10 streams." ; "Why not_recovered=1.0000? Maybe because at n=14, both_defected_run is actually 1?" ; "But score 0.9167 is all D/D? Wait 0.9167 is (1*11 + 0*?) actually over 24 rounds, all DD gives 1 per round = 24 points, average 1.0. 0.9167 is 22 points. So parent got mostly DD, not alternating. So maybe it never played C at n=14. Why? Because rng.random()<0.4 failed in all 10 streams? Unlikely."
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "Parent's score against four_D_TFT was 0.9167, meaning it got stuck in DD for entire probe (24 rounds). That's a big loss" ; "So we must fix that."
STRATEGY: The parent is a TFT-like strategy with forgiveness, exploit detection, and endgame defection. The trace simulates the parent against one_D_TFT, four_D_TFT, and sustained_D probes. It changes the parent by adding a long-defection probe/recovery rule, adjusting forgiveness thresholds, and adding adaptive cooldowns.

ORIGIN: NONE

So maybe even if it plays C, it doesn't achieve mutual cooperation because opponent is TFT?"; "But measured score 0.9167. So maybe rng didn't trigger C at n=14 in any of the 10 streams? Probability (0.6)^10 = 0.006. Unlikely but possible. Or maybe my analysis of round11 is wrong."
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "Parent got 0.9167. Big improvement."; "Parent got 2.6917. Similar."; "Parent got 2.3333. Same as parent!"
STRATEGY: Parent is a TFT-with-forgiveness strategy that cooperates at high cooperation rates, defects at high defection rates, and probes after long defection runs. The trace simulates the parent against one_D_TFT, four_D_TFT, four_D_ALLC, sustained_D, and periodic_D. It changes the probe logic to play two consecutive C's after a long defection run, adds an exploit rule for non-retaliators, and adjusts the my_def_run threshold.

--- PART 4/4 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "Parent got 0.9167 avg over 24 = 22 points. Over 100 rounds, parent would get ~91.7. Our strategy gets 99. Better." and "Parent got 2.6917 against four_D_ALLC, so they didn't exploit much either."
STRATEGY: Parent is a TFT-with-forgiveness strategy that probes long defection runs, occasionally tests high-cooperation opponents, and defects against high-defection opponents. The trace simulates it against ALLD, ALLC, one_D_TFT, four_D_TFT, four_D_ALLC, and periodic_D. It adds an exploit rule (switch to always D after two opponent cooperations following own defections) and keeps the existing probe/test schedule.
